about.background.title: Background & research problem
about.background.body: University complaints arrive as unstructured text. Identifying the topic, urgency, emotional tone, and responsible department can help administrators respond consistently. This project investigates these tasks for Kazakh, a language with comparatively limited NLP resources.
about.objectives.title: Research objectives
about.objectives.body: Compare classical, recurrent, multilingual Transformer, and Kazakh Transformer approaches on the same split; jointly predict four labels; evaluate held-out Macro-F1 and urgency errors; investigate confidence-aware routing with human review.
about.methodology.title: Dataset & methodology
about.methodology.body: The original study used 1,000 Kazakh university complaints: 700 training, 150 validation, and 150 testing examples. Seed 42, stratified by category × urgency. Text is normalized with Unicode NFC, selected invisible characters are removed, and whitespace is collapsed. Four targets have 3, 3, 3, and 6 classes. Neural models use the sum of four classification losses. Model selection and routing experiments use validation; final metrics use the held-out test set.
about.results.title: Architectures & main results
about.results.body: Linear SVM with character TF-IDF achieved the best mean Macro-F1 (0.9731). BiLSTM with attention achieved the best urgency F1 (0.9790). XLM-RoBERTa provides a multilingual comparison. KazRoBERTa achieved the best category F1 (0.9933) in the original study. This application now deploys the newly trained multilingual XLM-RoBERTa with four named classification heads. The application uses existing weights; it does not retrain models.
about.routing.title: Confidence-aware routing
about.routing.body: Routing confidence is the minimum of the maximum category, urgency, and department probabilities; tone is excluded. Manual review is required when confidence < 0.75 OR P(high urgency) ≥ 0.30. Potential urgency sets a high operational review priority independently of the model’s predicted urgency. The 4 / 24 / 72-hour SLA suggestions are research examples, not official policy. Human edits and original predictions are stored separately with change history.
about.limitations.title: Limitations & responsible AI
about.limitations.body: The dataset is small and has similar textual patterns across splits. The original study used a non-group-aware split. The multilingual export groups translations by original complaint ID; synthetic mixed-language results still do not establish real-world performance. Softmax scores are uncalibrated. Critical urgency can be missed even with high confidence. Local storage is not encrypted by this app, and there is no access-control layer. Use anonymized demonstration text, protect the device, and avoid sharing exported sensitive records. This tool supports human judgment and cannot autonomously resolve critical safety incidents.
about.future.title: Future improvements
about.future.body: Larger consented datasets, group-aware and multi-university evaluation, multiple training seeds, probability calibration, urgency-sensitive objectives, robustness to code-switching and spelling variation, proper authentication, encryption and retention controls, and institution-approved routing policies.
